transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

I keep avoiding anything that reminds me of my old job. Office buildings, security talks, networking events near work sites—I just dodge them. And if someone starts asking about the day it happened, I usually make an excuse and leave.
Could you share what happened on that day at your old job?

I remember seeing the gun, and then there’s just… nothing for a while. I can tell you all the mistakes they said I made afterward, every one of them, but the confrontation right after I saw it is blank. I’ve tried to put it together, but I can’t.
About how long ago did this event at your old job happen?
About a year and seven months ago—since I was fired after the armed incident.
Aside from avoiding reminders, do you ever experience unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the incident popping into your mind?
Yes. It can hit me out of nowhere—washing dishes, or driving past a warehouse gate. The scene just comes back so sharply I can hear people panicking, and my chest tightens like I’m right back there.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experienced an armed incident involving a firearm at their previous job over a year and a half ago, fulfilling the criterion for exposure to a traumatic stressor. Following this event, the patient exhibits persistent intrusive re-experiencing (flashbacks with vivid auditory recall and physiologic distress), marked avoidance of trauma-related reminders and conversations, and localized dissociative amnesia regarding the confrontation itself, consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder.

confirmed_symptoms: Spontaneous, vivid flashbacks where the scene abruptly returns
Physiological reactivity (chest tightening) and auditory re-experiencing (hearing people panicking)
Avoidance of trauma-related places, topics, and cues (office buildings, security talks, networking events)
Avoidance of conversations concerning the traumatic event
Dissociative amnesia for key aspects of the traumatic confrontation after seeing the weapon

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have persisted for approximately 1 year and 7 months following the armed incident.
additional_requirements: Exposure to actual or threatened death/serious injury during an armed workplace encounter
